title: MakeMyTrip India Gets SEBI Approval For IPO, Could Raise Over $1 Bn
summary: MakeMyTrip India gets SEBI approval for IPO to raise over $1 billion

sentences: MakeMyTrip's India arm has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to proceed with its initial public offering (IPO), marking a step towards the online travel aggregator's domestic stock market listing.
MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd had confidentially filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI in July 2026.
The market regulator issued its final observations on November 6, allowing the company to move ahead with preparations for the public issue, as per a media report.
The proposed IPO is expected to be an offer for sale (OFS), involving equity shares held by its parent company MakeMyTrip Ltd and ibibo Group Holdings.
The issue could raise more than USD 1 billion, according to earlier reports.
MakeMyTrip acquired ibibo Group in October 2016 through an all-stock transaction valued at approximately USD 720 million.
Following the proposed listing, MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd will continue to remain a subsidiary of the Nasdaq-listed parent company.
Its financial performance will also continue to be consolidated with the parent entity's results, according to a regulatory filing.
The domestic listing is expected to improve the company's brand visibility and strengthen its ability to attract and retain talent in India's competitive technology sector.
MakeMyTrip's India Listing Plans MakeMyTrip listed on the Nasdaq in 2010, when the US capital markets offered a more mature listing environment for technology companies compared with India.
Since then, India's public markets have expanded their presence in the new-age technology segment, with more than 70 technology companies entering the public markets and raising capital through IPOs.
In 2026, companies including Rentomojo, Shiprocket, Fractal and Shadowfax have made their stock market debuts.
MakeMyTrip first indicated its plans for an Indian listing in March 2026 as part of its strategy to strengthen its domestic market presence.
Ahead of the proposed IPO, the company has undertaken several business restructuring initiatives.
It merged its subsidiary RedBus with its Indian entity and expanded its portfolio through investments and acquisitions.
These include minority investments in visa processing platform Atlys and holiday packages company Flamingo Transworld.
The company also acquired a controlling stake in carpooling startup Quick Ride to expand its presence in the mobility segment.

MakeMyTrip's Financial Performance MakeMyTrip returned to profitability in Q2 FY27, reporting a consolidated net profit of USD 1.8 million against a net loss of USD 5.7 million in the corresponding quarter last year.
Revenue increased 2.5 per cent year-on-year to USD 235.2 million from USD 229.3 million in Q2 FY26.
For FY26, however, the company's net profit declined 45.8 per cent year-on-year to USD 51.7 million, while revenue increased 6.7 per cent to USD 1.04 billion.
MakeMyTrip operates across several online travel booking categories, including flights, hotels, holiday packages, buses and other travel-related services.
It competes with platforms such as EaseMyTrip, ixigo and Cleartrip, along with traditional travel agencies.

The proposed Indian listing comes as MakeMyTrip looks to strengthen its domestic operations and expand its presence across travel and mobility services while retaining its Nasdaq-listed parent structure.
